grammar_points.name: second_conditional
grammar_points.pattern: If + Subject + Past-Simple, Subject + would + Verb-infinitive

examples.sentence: If I had a question, I would ask the teacher.
If they didn't understand, I would explain it again.
If the price were lower, I would buy more fruit.
If the parent called, I would answer immediately.
If I had time, I would try a new hobby.

common_mistakes.wrong: If I have a question, I would ask.
common_mistakes.correct: If I had a question, I would ask.

common_mistakes.wrong: If the price was lower, I will buy more.
common_mistakes.correct: If the price were lower, I would buy more.

examples.sentence: I've been teaching here for ten years.
We've been preparing this lesson since morning.
My colleague has been discussing the schedule with the headteacher.
They have been complaining about the delay.
The parent has been waiting on the phone.

common_mistakes.wrong: I have taught here since morning. (when emphasizing the ongoing duration)
common_mistakes.correct: I have been teaching here since morning.

common_mistakes.wrong: He has being teaching English.
common_mistakes.correct: He has been teaching English.

examples.sentence: I wish I could improve my vocabulary faster.
I wish the safety procedure were simpler.
I wish you didn't make that mistake.
examples.context: expressing gentle regret on a task

examples.sentence: She wishes she had a vegetarian option.
I wish I apologized to my colleague yesterday.

common_mistakes.wrong: I wish I can speak English.
common_mistakes.correct: I wish I could speak English.

common_mistakes.wrong: He wishes he has more money.
common_mistakes.correct: He wishes he had more money.

examples.sentence: He said that he was sick.
The parent said she was very happy with the progress.
My colleague said he had already sent the email.
The doctor said that I needed medicine.
She said she preferred vegetarian food.

common_mistakes.wrong: He said he is sick yesterday.
common_mistakes.correct: He said he was sick yesterday.

common_mistakes.wrong: She said me she liked it. (when using say)
common_mistakes.correct: She told me she liked it. OR She said she liked it.

examples.sentence: The safety procedure must be followed by everyone.
The reservation should be confirmed before Friday.
The ticket can be bought at the airport.
The medicine should be taken after meals.
The lesson plans could be improved next week.

common_mistakes.wrong: The safety procedure must follow by everyone.
common_mistakes.correct: The safety procedure must be followed by everyone.

common_mistakes.wrong: The reservation should be confirm before Friday.
common_mistakes.correct: The reservation should be confirmed before Friday.

grammar_points.name: although_however_despite
grammar_points.pattern: Although + clause, clause | However, clause | Despite + noun/-ing, clause

examples.sentence: Although the lesson was long, the students enjoyed it.
The food was expensive. However, the quality was excellent.
Despite the delay, we arrived on time.
Although I apologised, she was still upset.
Despite the bad weather, we had a productive meeting.

common_mistakes.wrong: Although it was long but they enjoyed it.
common_mistakes.correct: Although it was long, they enjoyed it.

common_mistakes.wrong: Despite of the delay, we arrived.
common_mistakes.correct: Despite the delay, we arrived.

grammar_points.name: purpose_so_that
grammar_points.pattern: clause + so that + clause | clause + in order to + verb

examples.sentence: I studied hard so that I could pass the exam.
We left early in order to arrive on time.
I wrote a report so that the principal could review it.
She took medicine in order to feel better.
I called the parent so that they would know.

common_mistakes.wrong: I studied hard for pass the exam.
common_mistakes.correct: I studied hard in order to pass the exam.

common_mistakes.wrong: I left early so that arrive on time.
common_mistakes.correct: I left early so that I could arrive on time.

examples.sentence: I had my car fixed last week.
She had her hair cut before the meeting.
We had the report printed by the office.
I need to have my eyes checked by the doctor.
He had his phone repaired at the shop.

common_mistakes.wrong: I had fixed my car. (meaning someone else did it)
common_mistakes.correct: I had my car fixed.

common_mistakes.wrong: I have the report print.
common_mistakes.correct: I had the report printed.

grammar_points.name: complex_questions
grammar_points.pattern: Do you know / Could you tell me + wh-word + subject + verb?

examples.sentence: Do you know where the nearest hospital is?
Could you tell me what time the meeting starts?
I wonder if the reservation has been confirmed.
Do you have any idea how long the delay will be?
Can you explain why the student was absent?

common_mistakes.wrong: Do you know where is the hospital?
common_mistakes.correct: Do you know where the hospital is?

common_mistakes.wrong: Can you tell me what time does it start?
common_mistakes.correct: Can you tell me what time it starts?

grammar_points.name: linking_words
grammar_points.pattern: Furthermore / Moreover / On the other hand / Nevertheless + , + clause

examples.sentence: Furthermore, we need to prepare the worksheets.
On the other hand, the students might prefer a project.
In addition, the principal has approved the new schedule.
Nevertheless, we should continue with the original plan.
Moreover, the feedback from parents has been very positive.

common_mistakes.wrong: Furthermore we need to prepare.
common_mistakes.correct: Furthermore, we need to prepare.

common_mistakes.wrong: On other hand, they might prefer.
common_mistakes.correct: On the other hand, they might prefer.
